auth.apple.confirm.title: Read this first
auth.apple.disclosure:
⚠️ Not officially supported by Apple. The two tokens you're about to paste belong to Apple's web player (music.apple.com):
  · Apple may change or revoke them at any time, and then they stop working — just run capy auth login apple again
  · Accessing Apple Music with a third-party tool is at your own risk under Apple's terms of service
  · capy only shows you how to copy them by hand; it never reads your browser's data
  · When capy writes, tracks added to a playlist may also be added to your Apple Music library (depending on your Apple Music settings; this is Apple's behavior); capy only writes to playlists you created

auth.apple.guide:
Copy the tokens from Apple's web player (about 1 minute):
  1. Open https://music.apple.com in a browser and log in
  2. Open DevTools (F12 / ⌥⌘I) → Network tab, filter by "amp-api"
  3. Click any song or playlist, then click any amp-api request → Request Headers
  4. Copy the value of authorization (the whole string; with or without "Bearer ") → developer token
  5. Copy the value of media-user-token → user token

auth.apple.wizard.guide_title: Copy the tokens from the web player

auth.spotify.app_steps:
Spotify's policy limits each app to 5 users, so you need your own app:
1. Open https://developer.spotify.com/dashboard
2. Create app, any name
3. Redirect URI (copy it exactly): http://127.0.0.1:8888/callback
4. Tick Web API → Save
5. Copy the Client ID into the next field

cmd.auth.status.short: Show each platform's authorization status (offline check; use capy doctor to verify online)

cmd.doctor.short: Check your setup and connections (one stop for BYO credential problems)
cmd.drive.init.flag.dry_run: only list the files to create, don't upload (exits 2 if there is anything to create)
cmd.drive.init.flag.from_local: restore the files missing on Drive from this machine's state.db (currently the only mode)
cmd.drive.init.long:
The way out after pl pull stops with exit 3 because Drive is incomplete. Only creates the files missing on Drive and never overwrites existing ones (files still on Drive win),
and leaves the local cache alone; other devices' dev__ files are not uploaded on their behalf (each device writes only its own; the next time that device pulls, it has no base and only adds, never removes).
First lists the files to create (without a TTY: headerless TSV with columns action, file) and uploads only after you confirm; exit 0 = done or nothing missing, 1 = error, 2 = pending (--dry-run, no TTY without --yes, or cancelled).
The confirmation shows the Google account you are logged in to: if it's the wrong account, this command would upload all your playlist data (playlists and track mappings) to someone else's appdata.
cmd.drive.init.short: Restore the files missing from the Drive appdata using this machine's state.db (the only command allowed to write while the appdata is empty or incomplete)
cmd.drive.short: Maintenance commands for the Google Drive appdata
cmd.export.long:
Reads only the local state.db and never touches Drive, the network or the keychain. Prints one JSON object: the keys are the file names on Drive (manifest.json, tracks.json,
pl__<pid>.json, dev__<device_id>.json) and the values are those files' contents, byte-for-byte the same as on Drive. The output is the same with or without a TTY.
With no local data it exits 1 and prints nothing to stdout (so capy export > backup.json never silently writes an empty file).
cmd.export.short: Print this machine's canonical data to stdout (the Drive files merged into one JSON; an escape hatch that doesn't depend on Drive)
cmd.history.clear.short: Clear recent history (the playlist cache is kept)
cmd.history.short: Recent searches and plays (local cache, used by completion and the picker)
cmd.migrate.flag.dry_run: only list what would be moved; creates no playlist and touches neither the platforms nor Drive (exits 2 if there is anything to move)
cmd.migrate.flag.from: source platform ({ids}); picked interactively in a terminal if omitted
cmd.migrate.flag.to: target platform, or <platform>:<existing playlist ID or name>; a platform alone creates a new playlist named after the source (Spotify / Apple Music); picked interactively in a terminal if omitted
cmd.migrate.flag.yes: skip the confirmation (for cron / pipelines); unmatched tracks aren't reviewed on the spot
cmd.migrate.long:
Copies a playlist from the --from platform to the --to platform, without chaining pl link / pull / resolve / push yourself. --to with only a platform = create a private playlist there named after the source
(Spotify and Apple Music can create playlists, local can't); --to <platform>:<playlist> = add to an existing playlist. With no arguments in a terminal, it asks step by step (source platform → playlist → target platform → an existing playlist or a new one);
without a TTY, give the playlist and --from / --to.

Order: the target's existing order is the prefix, and the source's tracks follow in the source's order; tracks the target already has (same platform id or same ISRC) are skipped, and duplicates within the source are kept only once.
The source is never touched; the target only gets additions — if the target has unsynced removals / reorders / renames, it stops with exit 3: run capy pl sync first.
Each track is matched by ISRC lookup first, then by fuzzy matching (≥85 is automatic); unmatched tracks aren't pushed this time, the table says so, and in a terminal you can review them on the spot.
One table (without a TTY: TSV with columns dir action provider playlist pos cid provider_id title artists reason reason_code; dir ∈ pull / migrate / push; reason is for people and follows the language, reason_code is a fixed code for scripts), one confirmation;
--dry-run only lists (exits 2 if there is anything to move, creates no playlist); without a TTY and without --yes it also exits 2. The playlist on the target platform is created only after you confirm.
Afterwards only the target is linked to capy's master copy (the source isn't linked: a one-time copy); to keep them in sync, the last lines give the pl link + pl sync commands.
local can only add to an existing file (--to local:<file name>). Tracks moved into Apple Music may also be added to your Apple Music library (depending on your Apple Music settings; this is Apple's behavior); on Apple, capy only writes to playlists you created, and songs no longer available in the store can't be moved: the table may still list them, and capy warns when it re-reads the playlist after writing.
cmd.migrate.short: Move a playlist from one platform to another (as a new playlist or into an existing one); keeps the order, never deletes the source, only adds
cmd.migrate.use: [source playlist ID or name] --from <platform> --to <platform>[:<existing playlist ID or name>]
cmd.pl.dedup.flag.dry_run: only list the changes; touches neither the platforms nor Drive (exits 2 if there are changes)
cmd.pl.dedup.flag.force: override the deletion threshold (dedup and push counted separately); removed copies are pushed to the playlist's other linked platforms in the same command, so run --dry-run first
cmd.pl.dedup.flag.provider: run the pull / push halves only for this provider (default: every provider the playlist is linked to); deduping the master copy is the same for all platforms
cmd.pl.dedup.long:
A duplicate is the same platform id or the same ISRC (a single and its album version count as one track). The first occurrence is kept and later ones are removed; the rest keep their relative order.

<provider>:<playlist ID or name>: reads the platform playlist directly and only reports (without a TTY: headerless TSV with columns pos id title artists reason reason_code; pos starts at 0; reason is for people and follows the language, reason_code is a fixed code for scripts); doesn't touch Drive
and needs no link; exits 0 whether or not there are duplicates. To have capy remove them, link the playlist to a master copy and use the form below. --yes / --force / --dry-run / --provider are errors with this form.

A canonical playlist (name|pid; with no argument in a terminal, opens a picker): one pl sync round with an extra step in the middle — pull first (the platforms' current state goes into the master copy),
dedup the master copy, then push to remove the extra copies from the platforms capy can write to. One table (without a TTY: TSV with columns dir action provider playlist pos cid provider_id title artists reason reason_code,
dir ∈ pull / dedup / push; pos in dedup rows is the position in the master copy) and one confirmation; exit codes as for pl sync (0 = no changes or applied, 1 = error, 2 = pending, 3 = safety check).
Nothing is written when neither the master copy nor the platforms checked this time have duplicates (other changes the pull half sees are left for pl sync; platforms not selected by --provider or unreadable are not checked this time, and stderr says so).
The deletion threshold applies to dedup and push separately (>10 tracks, or >30% and >3 tracks); --force overrides it. Copies left on platforms capy can't write to are listed on stderr for you to delete by hand; the next pull won't add them back to the master copy.
cmd.pl.dedup.short: Remove duplicate tracks from a playlist (same platform id or same ISRC; keeps the first copy, the rest stay in order)
cmd.pl.link.flag.create: create an empty playlist on the platform with the master copy's name, then link it; the second argument is then just the platform, without ":" (e.g. spotify); works with Spotify and Apple Music, not local
cmd.pl.link.short: Link a master copy to a platform playlist (creating the master copy if it doesn't exist; only explicit links count. With no arguments in a terminal, a three-step picker asks)
cmd.pl.pull.flag.dry_run: only list the changes, don't write (exits 2 if there are any)
cmd.pl.pull.flag.force: override the removal threshold (>10 tracks, or >30% and >3 tracks); single playlist only, not with --all; doesn't let an incomplete Drive through
cmd.pl.pull.flag.provider: pull only the links to this provider (default: every provider the playlist is linked to)
cmd.pl.pull.flag.yes: skip the confirmation (for cron / pipes); doesn't let an incomplete Drive through
cmd.pl.pull.long:
Platform → master copy → Drive (spec §6.1, §6.5). The change set is printed first (when not a TTY, as headerless TSV: action provider playlist pos cid provider_id title artists reason reason_code; reason is for people and follows the language, reason_code is a fixed code for scripts),
and written only after you confirm; Drive is written first, then SQLite. Exit codes: 0 no changes or applied, 1 error, 2 changes pending (--dry-run, not a TTY without --yes, cancelled),
3 stopped by a safety check (Drive incomplete; removing >10 tracks, or >30% and >3 tracks). --yes skips the confirmation and only --force overrides the removal threshold; neither lets an incomplete Drive through.
cmd.pl.pull.short: Platform → master copy → Drive: list the changes, write only after you confirm (spec §6.1)
cmd.pl.push.flag.dry_run: only list the changes; touch neither the platforms nor Drive (exits 2 if there are changes)
cmd.pl.push.flag.force: override the removal threshold (>10 tracks, or >30% and >3 tracks); single playlist only, not with --all; doesn't override the two preconditions
cmd.pl.push.flag.provider: push only the link to this provider (default: every provider the playlist is linked to)
cmd.pl.push.flag.yes: skip the confirmation (for cron / pipelines); doesn't override the two preconditions
cmd.pl.push.long:
Master copy → platforms (spec §6.5.2). Mirrors pl pull: the change set is printed first (without a TTY it's a headerless TSV with the same columns as pull; action adds skip = in the master copy but not on the platform,
with no mapping for this platform yet — run capy resolve first), and the platform is written only after you confirm; then capy re-reads the platform, records it as the base, and writes Drive (the master copy's content doesn't change).
exit code: 0 no changes or applied, 1 error (including a partial write to the platform: the message says how many tracks were written; run push again to finish), 2 pending, 3 safety check.
Two preconditions (--force doesn't override them): this device has pulled this platform playlist (otherwise the platform could be wiped); the platform has no changes that haven't been pulled (otherwise you'd overwrite what you just changed there) —
run capy pl pull or capy pl sync first. Spotify playlists with local files can't be pushed yet. The removal threshold is the same as pull's (relative to the platform's track count); --force overrides it and only works with a single playlist.
When counting changes by stdout lines, leave out the skip rows.
cmd.pl.push.short: Master copy → platforms: list the changes, write only after you confirm (spec §6.5.2)
cmd.pl.show.short: Show a playlist's tracks (with no argument in a terminal, opens a picker)
cmd.pl.sync.flag.dry_run: only list the changes for the whole round; touch neither the platforms nor Drive (exits 2 if there are changes)
cmd.pl.sync.flag.force: override the removal threshold (checked separately for pull and push); also pushes those removals to the playlist's other linked platforms, so use --dry-run first; single playlist only, not with --all
cmd.pl.sync.flag.provider: run the round for this provider only (default: every provider the playlist is linked to)
cmd.pl.sync.long:
Under one lock, each playlist is first pulled from each platform (platform → master copy), then pushed to each platform (master copy → platform); --provider runs just one platform.
The change set is printed all at once (without a TTY it's a headerless TSV: dir action provider playlist pos cid provider_id title artists reason reason_code; dir ∈ pull / push; reason is for people and follows the language, reason_code is a fixed code for scripts), and you confirm once;
with --dry-run the push half is projected from the master copy as it would be after the pull, so you see the whole round. The threshold is checked per (playlist, platform); exit codes are the same as pl pull / pl push.
The push half reuses the platform playlists the pull half just read instead of reading them again; the platforms are written before Drive, and if writing Drive then fails, the message says the platforms were already changed.
When --provider points to a platform that can't be written (e.g. another device's local library playlist), sync only pulls and says so on stderr; when one playlist can't be pushed to one platform (e.g. it has local files), only that push half is skipped,
not the whole round (a cron sync --all won't get stuck on one playlist). The removal threshold still stops the whole round; with --force, removals absorbed by the pull half are pushed in the same command
to every platform linked to this playlist — check with --dry-run first.
cmd.pl.sync.short: One round of pull, then push: one table, one confirmation (spec decision 31)
cmd.pl.unlink.short: Unlink a master copy from a platform playlist (the master copy is left as is; with no arguments in a terminal, a two-step picker asks)
cmd.prev.short: Go back to the previous track
cmd.resolve.flag.dry_run: only list, don't write (exits 2 if there are mappings to write automatically; can't be combined with --review)
cmd.resolve.flag.provider: only process this provider (default: every provider the playlists are linked to)
cmd.resolve.flag.review: review the queue item by item in a terminal (without a TTY: prints the queue and exits 2; can't be combined with --dry-run)
cmd.resolve.flag.yes: skip the confirmation (for cron / pipelines); with --review, also agrees to merges
cmd.resolve.long:
For each linked (playlist, provider), finds the tracks in items that have no mapping for that provider: first an ISRC lookup (confidence 95), otherwise
a fuzzy match on title + artists + duration (0–100). ≥85 is written automatically (the same path as pl pull: pull.lock, the incomplete-Drive gate, Drive first, then SQLite);
the rest are printed as the review queue — a candidate that already belongs to another cid always goes to the queue, because only a person decides a merge.
Without a TTY the output is TSV: action cid provider provider_id confidence source title artists reason reason_code (action ∈ map | review | conflict; reason is for people and follows the language, reason_code is a fixed code for scripts).
Exit code: 0 = nothing to write or written (still 0 when the queue has items), 1 = error, 2 = automatic mappings pending but not confirmed (--dry-run, no TTY without --yes, or cancelled).
--review reviews the queue item by item in a terminal (accept / skip / search manually / pin as unavailable / keep the current one); without a TTY it only prints the queue and exits 2;
decisions are written together at the end, and Esc / Ctrl-C midway writes nothing from this run (automatic mappings included) and exits 2.
cmd.resolve.pin.flag.yes: merge right away when the id already belongs to another cid (without a TTY and without this flag, exits 2 and writes nothing)
cmd.resolve.pin.short: Pin a cid's id on a platform by hand (none = the platform doesn't have this track); merges the two when the id already belongs to another cid
cmd.resolve.short: Map canonical tracks to their ids on each platform (ISRC lookup → fuzzy match; ≥85 is written automatically, the rest go to the review queue)
cmd.root.flag.port: port for --web (default 0 = any free port; 8888, 80 and 443 are not allowed)
cmd.root.flag.web: use capy from your browser: binds to 127.0.0.1 only and prints a one-time URL at startup
cmd.root.short: Cross-platform music CLI: search, playback control, playlist sync
cmd.update.flag.dev: update to the latest commit on main (built from source; needs the Go toolchain)
cmd.update.long:
Update capy itself.

With no flags: asks GitHub Releases for the latest release, downloads this platform's file, verifies its SHA-256
against checksums.txt and runs the new binary's --version to make sure it works, and only then replaces the running
binary. The checksum only proves the download is complete (releases are not signed).
Running it from a dev build (built with go install or --dev) switches you to the release.

--dev: asks GitHub for the latest commit on the main branch, rebuilds from source with go install, then replaces the
running binary (needs the Go toolchain; the first run downloads dependencies, about 20 seconds).
cmd.update.short: Update capy itself (latest release; --dev builds the latest commit on main)

dedup.pulled_only.other: Applied {count} pull changes (nothing to remove from the master copy)

google.guide:
Create your own Google OAuth client (free, about 5 minutes) — this binary has no built-in client (builds from go install never include one):
  1. https://console.cloud.google.com → create a project → APIs & Services → enable "Google Drive API"
  2. Google Auth platform → Branding: fill in the app name and support email; for Audience choose External
  3. Data Access: add only these three scopes — openid, userinfo.email, drive.appdata (adding Gmail or similar triggers a security assessment)
  4. Create an OAuth client of type "Desktop app"; the secret is shown only once, when it's created, so copy it right away
  5. ⚠️ Under Audience, click "Publish app" to move to In production — if it stays in Testing, the refresh token expires after 7 days and you'll be logged out without warning
  6. Paste the Client ID and Client secret below
google.login.done: ✅ Google authorization complete: {who} (client source: {source}; token saved in the keychain)
google.login.waiting: Finish the Google authorization in your browser… (within 180s; tick all three permissions)
google.secret_prompt.body:
Config still has a Google client ID ({client_id}), but its secret isn't in the keychain (capy auth logout google deletes it).
Paste the secret, or just press Enter to try without one (acceptance check G-0 will settle whether a Desktop client must send a secret).

resolve.reason.isrc_conflict: different ids seen for the same ISRC: {ids}; keep in --review pins the current mapping
resolve.review.confirm_merge: This {provider} id already belongs to cid {other}: merge {cid} with it? (The lexicographically smaller cid wins and every playlist item is repointed to it)
resolve.review.opt.keep: Keep the current mapping {id} (you confirmed it; won't ask again)
resolve.review.opt.none: This platform doesn't have it (pin as unavailable)
resolve.review.pick_title: Pick a track to pin (Esc skips)
resolve.review.search_failed: Search failed, skipping this one for now: {err}
resolve.review.title:
[{pos}/{total}] {title} — {artists} ({duration})
{provider}: {reason}
store.err.no_db: there is no state.db on this machine
store.err.schema_mismatch: this machine's state.db has a different schema version from this capy

sync.confirm.one: Apply the {count} change above ({pulls} pulled to Drive, {pushes} pushed to platforms)?
sync.confirm.other: Apply the {count} changes above ({pulls} pulled to Drive, {pushes} pushed to platforms)?

sync.confirm_force: --force: removals will spread to every platform this playlist is linked to. {prompt}
sync.err.force_with_all: --force works with a single playlist only (capy pl sync <name> --force), not with --all
sync.next: run capy pl sync again (its pull half absorbs what was already pushed as platform changes, so nothing is duplicated)
sync.next_after_half: then run capy pl sync again
update.dev.building: Latest on main is {sha} ({date}); you have {version}. Building (the first run downloads dependencies, about 20 seconds)…
update.err.checksum_mismatch: SHA-256 mismatch (incomplete download, or the release file was replaced): {got} ≠ {want} in {checksums}
update.err.github_parse: couldn't parse the GitHub API response: {err}
update.err.github_rate_limit: GitHub API rate limit reached (60 requests an hour without authentication); try again later
update.err.missing_asset: release v{version} is missing {name} (the file for this platform, {os}/{arch}) or {checksums}; see https://github.com/{repo}/releases
update.err.no_checksum_line: {checksums} has no line for {name}; refusing to install
update.err.no_go: go not found: --dev builds from source and needs the Go toolchain (https://go.dev/dl/)
update.err.no_release: there is no release yet (the maintainer hasn't published one); for now, capy update --dev updates to the latest commit on main
update.err.no_sha: couldn't parse the GitHub API response: no sha
update.err.place_new: putting the new binary in place: {err}
update.err.tempdir: can't create a temporary directory in {dir} (capy needs write access there to replace itself): {err}
update.err.verify_failed: the new binary failed its self-check (the old one is untouched): {err}
update.err.version_mismatch: {bin} --version printed {got}, which doesn't contain the expected {want}
update.release.downloading: Latest release is v{version} (you have {current}); downloading {name}…
update.release.downloading_from_dev: Latest release is v{version} (you're on a dev build, {current}; switching to the release); downloading {name}…
